summary.oneLiner: We offer a diverse range of high-quality hand-crafted gold jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat.
summary.business: We operate an asset-light business, wherein Karigars hand craft jewellery according to Client’s requirement and act as principal contractor, managing the design, material sourcing, and finished Jewellery making process for our clients. We offer a diverse range of high-quality hand-crafted gold jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat. It is essentially an asset-light model in which we offer our expertise in jewellery design, craftsmanship and timely delivery of our products to all our customers who are spread PAN India.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light, non-integrated wholesale model with no backward manufacturing integration and no forward retail integration. The Company describes itself as a wholesale (B2B) player in hand-crafted gold jewellery that acts as principal contractor, managing design, material sourcing and the finished jewellery making process for its clients. Under the heading 'Capacity' the RHP states: 'The manufacturing process is predominantly outsourced to skilled job workers, commonly referred to as Karigars... Hence, we don't have any in-house manufacturing capacity.' Backward: the Company procures pure gold (995 or 999 purity) from bullion dealers / gold merchants, all BIS-marked with the refiner's bar number on the bar and on the invoice; raw material purchases by type (as printed, % of Total Purchase) were Gold Bar 93.27% / 87.12% / 85.61%, Gold Ornaments 6.63% / 12.80% / 14.30%, Stones nil / 0.00% / 0.09%, Miscellaneous 0.10% / 0.08% / 0.00% for FY 2026 / FY 2025 / FY 2024, with total raw material cost of Rs. 15,009.92 million, Rs. 13,231.06 million and Rs. 9,928.30 million respectively; the RHP states the Company does not enter into long-term agreements with suppliers. Production: 72 jobworkers were associated during Fiscal 2026 (87 in Fiscal 2025, 90 in Fiscal 2024), of whom 66 have executed the Company's prescribed agreements, giving access to multiple Karigars; jobworker attrition was 17.24% (Fiscal 2026), 3.33% (Fiscal 2025) and 1.10% (Fiscal 2024); major jobworker manufacturing units are located in Mumbai, Maharashtra. In-house functions retained are design (3 designers in each of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024), inventory management, purity/metal-pin testing, finishing, final quality control, labelling and photography, and app/online listing - a nine-step process ending with mixed inventory held at the office for clients visiting in person. Forward: the Company does not operate retail showrooms; its Corporate and Non-Corporate Clients resell through their own retail showrooms or online channels. Its mobile application on Google Play Store and App Store is used to showcase designs to clients and is expressly not meant for sale of products. Operations are focused exclusively on domestic markets within India, with a customer network spanning 21 states and 4 union territories; customer counts were 418 (Fiscal 2026), 457 (Fiscal 2025) and 448 (Fiscal 2024), split into repeat customers of 334 / 291 / 279 and new customers of 84 / 166 / 169. Inventory intensity: inventory was Rs. 2,399.58 million / Rs. 1,615.84 million / Rs. 1,314.26 million (62.06% / 66.28% / 75.48% of current assets) with inventory days of 54 / 42 / 45 and inventory turnover of 6.80 / 8.69 / 8.08 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024; working capital facilities were Rs. 1,670.00 million as at March 31, 2026, and the Company intends to utilise Rs. 380.00 million of Net Proceeds towards working capital and Rs. 1,580 million towards repayment of working capital debt. Product returns were Rs. 1,177.56 million / Rs. 733.98 million / Rs. 462.72 million, being 7.22% / 5.23% / 4.36% of revenue from operations for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, which the RHP attributes primarily to customer preference-related adjustments rather than quality issues. Headcount: 46 permanent employees as of May 31, 2026 (Executive Directors and KMP 4, Accounts and Finance 4, Administration 16, Sales and Marketing 5, Designing and Client Servicing 11, Quality 6), against 44 / 33 / 31 payroll employees at the end of Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 with employee attrition of 10.39% / 6% / 0%. Insurance covering the gold inventory includes a Jewellers Block Protector Policy no. 48057391 from Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Company Limited providing coverage up to Rs. 4,762.50 million, valid to October 28, 2026.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: The RHP discloses seasonality as a distinct risk factor (Risk Factor 15): 'Our income and sales are subject to seasonal fluctuations and lower income in a peak season may have a disproportionate effect on our results of operations.' It states the business is subject to significant seasonal fluctuations affecting sales, income and overall financial performance, and that historically the demand for gold jewellery is driven by cultural events, festivals and wedding seasons which vary through the year. Festivals cited elsewhere in the RHP include Akshaya Tritiya, Navratri/Durga Puja, Gudi Padwa, Gurupushyamrut, Diwali and Dhanteras. The Company states its revenues and operations tend to experience peaks and troughs based on the timing of these events; that seasonal fluctuations also affect inventory management, since a large build-up of inventory ahead of peak periods can leave excess stock while insufficient inventory can cause missed sales; and that seasonality creates cash-flow volatility because off-season months generate lower sales and strain working capital. Risk Factor 33 adds that the Company operates in a business environment where orders are generally received based on customer and seasonal demand, and it plans inventory and estimates sales based on the forecast, demand and requirements for forthcoming festivals and seasons. The rural-demand-post-harvest (September-November) and gold-price observations in the same risk factor are attributed to the commissioned CareEdge Report and are not the issuer's own disclosure. No quarter-wise or month-wise revenue seasonality table is printed.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our business and the demand for our product is reliant on the success of our customers’ products with end consumers, and any decline in the demand for the end-products could have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
- Jewellers, particularly smaller players, need to maintain large gold inventories to meet customer demand.
- Our customers, including Corporate Clients, further sell our products to end use customers.
- For further details in relation to our customers, see “Our Business” on page 194.
- Any material downturn in any of our customers services, as a result of increased competition, seasonality of demand, our customers’ failure to successfully market their products or to compete effectively, loss of market share, macroeconomic conditions in the markets of key end-customers, regulatory action, litigation, pricing fluctuation or other factors may impact us.
- Any of these factors could have an adverse effect on the end-use customers and sales of our product could decline substantially which could adversely affect our profitability and result of operations.
- Additionally, the prices of gold and diamonds at a particular time also affect the decision of our customers to purchase jewellery.
- Most of our end-customers of our customers are individuals who purchase jewellery for personal use and who are generally less financially resilient than corporate entities.
